newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL- PACKERS' SIX-TIME PRO BOWL TIGHT END KEITH JACKSON RETIRES.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL- PACKERS' SIX-TIME PRO BOWL TIGHT END KEITH JACKSON RETIRES.

text.p: Six-time Pro Bowler Keith Jackson of the Super Bowl champion Green Bay Packers, one of the NFL's most productive tight ends over the past decade, retired Monday.

Jackson, who turns 32 on April 19, was the active leader among tight ends with 441 receptions. He had more touchdowns (49) since 1988 than any other tight end and closed his career with 5,283 receiving yards.
"You've got to know your journey's over, and basically, at this time of my life, it's over," said Jackson at a news conference.

"It's a sad day, because all those friendships I value and hold dear. This is an end to something I've done for so long, but fortunately I do have my mind on right, and I realise that one day it had to come to an end and that there is life after football."

Only one player, former Detroit Lions great Charlie Sanders, earned more Pro Bowl honours as a tight end with seven, and only one other, Steve Jordan of the Minnesota Vikings, has been a six-time honouree.
However, Jackson did leave the door open for a possible return.

"I guess I'll do like Michael Jordan and never say never," said Jackson. "I'll never go and play minor league baseball. I really do want to do some other things (but) I would never say the door's completely shut."
Jackson combined with Mark Chmura to give Green Bay the best tight end tandem in the NFL for the last two seasons.

At first, Jackson was unhappy with the trade that sent him from the Miami Dolphins to Green Bay in March of 1995 and refused to report. He spent the first six weeks of the season on the reserve/did not report list, but was finally convinced by Packers general manager Ron Wolf and coach Mike Holmgren to join the team.
"I was a little stubborn and bullheaded at first, and didn't want to come here," said Jackson.

"It turned out to be an outstanding time of my life, a great two years, to not only make friends, but to see how an organisation is really supposed to be run. Everywhere I go around the United States of America right now, I brag about what happens here in Green Bay."

Jackson played in nine regular-season games for Green Bay in 1995, primarily as a backup to Chmura, and had 13 catches for 142 yards and one touchdown. But Jackson shined in the 1995 playoffs, catching 12 passes for 223 yards and two touchdowns in two games.
He had four catches for 101 yards and a touchdown in Green Bay's stunning 27-17 divisional playoff win at San Francisco.

Jackson was an unrestricted free agent following the 1995 season, but elected to re-sign with Green Bay and helped the Packers win their first Super Bowl title since 1968 and earned Pro Bowl honours. He had 40 catches for 505 yards and a career-high 10 touchdowns during the regular season and added five catches for 44 yards in the postseason.
Jackson's 49 career touchdowns ranks third all-time among tight ends, behind Jerry Smith of the Washington Redskins with 60 and Dave Casper of the Oakland Raiders and Houston Oilers with 52.

Jackson, a first-round pick of the Philadelphia Eagles in 1988 out of Oklahoma, earned Pro Bowl honours three times with the Eagles (1988, 1989, 1990) and twice with the Miami Dolphins (1992 and 1993).
Jackson made an immediate impact for the Eagles, leading the team with 81 catches for 869 yards and was named as the only rookie starter for the NFC in the Pro Bowl.
Following four seasons in Philadelphia, Jackson signed as a free agent with Miami in 1992.
